title: Slouching Towards Bethlehem
author: Joan Didion
quote: The market overflows with the prerequisites of reformed life-styles: hardware for light shows, incense for the soul, instructions for a generation that does not know how to cook an egg.

title: The White Album
author: Joan Didion
quote: We tell ourselves stories in order to live.

title: The Case for Reparations
author: Ta-Nehisi Coates
quote: Two hundred fifty years of slavery. Ninety years of Jim Crow. Sixty years of separate but equal. Thirty-five years of racist housing policy. Until we reckon with our compounding moral debts, America will never be whole.

title: Notes of a Native Son
author: James Baldwin
quote: I imagine one of the reasons people cling to their hates so stubbornly is because they sense, once hate is gone, they will be forced to deal with pain.

title: Politics and the English Language
author: George Orwell
quote: Political language... is designed to make lies sound truthful and murder respectable, and to give an appearance of solidity to pure wind.

title: Consider the Lobster
author: David Foster Wallace
quote: Is it possible that future generations will regard our present agribusiness and eating practices in much the same way we now view Nero’s entertainments or Aztec sacrifices?

title: The Fire Next Time
author: James Baldwin
quote: Everything now, we must assume, is in our hands; we have no right to assume otherwise.

title: On Keeping a Notebook
author: Joan Didion
quote: I think we are well advised to keep on nodding terms with the people we used to be, whether we find them attractive company or not.

title: Looking Back on the Spanish War
author: George Orwell
quote: The very concept of objective truth is fading out of the world. Lies will pass into history.

title: A Supposedly Fun Thing I'll Never Do Again
author: David Foster Wallace
quote: I have seen 500 upscale Americans dance the Electric Slide. I have seen sunset look like a postcard from a postcard.
